findings.message: The new 'Setup MinGW path' step puts C:/mingw32/bin (the 32-bit toolchain) on PATH for both MinGW/GCC jobs, so the x86_64 job runs with the wrong toolchain on PATH. The step is gated only on `matrix.mingw == 'yes'`, which is true for both the x86_64 entry (mingw_prefix=C:/mingw64, line 132) and the x86_32 entry (mingw_prefix=C:/mingw32, line 144), and it runs `echo "C:/mingw32/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH` with a hardcoded path. godot-tools/windows.py:81-104 calls the compiler and linker by absolute prefix, but any tool found through PATH (helper DLLs, as/ld lookups, gcc-ar plugins) comes from the 32-bit install. The path should come from the matrix (for example `${{ matrix.msys }}`) or follow mingw_prefix.

The x86_32 GCC job may fail, or may build against an unintended toolchain, because it assumes a preinstalled C:/mingw32 on windows-2025 that nothing in the workflow installs or checks. The diff removes `msys2/setup-msys2@v2`, which installed `mingw-w64-${{matrix.msysenv}}-gcc` for each arch. Now the build relies only on `mingw_prefix=C:/mingw32` (line 144) and `C:/mingw64` (line 132). No step installs these toolchains or verifies they exist, and windows.py:82 just builds `prefix = env["mingw_prefix"] + "/bin/"` and calls `i686-w64-mingw32-g++`. If the runner image has no 32-bit MinGW at C:/mingw32, the release artefact godot-angle-static-x86_32-gcc-release is never produced.

The compiler that builds the shipped MinGW/GCC release libraries changes from MSYS2's packaged GCC to whatever version the windows-2025 image ships, unpinned. Its CRT may also differ from the 'MSVCRT' the artefacts are labelled with. The removed step installed `mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc` / `mingw-w64-i686-gcc` from the MSYS2 mingw64/mingw32 environments, which target MSVCRT. The new config just points `mingw_prefix` at C:/mingw64 and C:/mingw32 on `os: windows-2025`, so the toolchain version and runtime now follow runner-image updates. Nothing in the workflow records or checks which GCC or CRT is used, yet the job names (lines 125, 137) still claim '(MSVCRT)' and the release job publishes these artefacts.

The matrix keys `msys` and `msysenv` are now dead configuration that suggests an MSYS2 environment is still in use. After the diff, no step references `matrix.msys` or `matrix.msysenv`. Their only consumer was the removed `msys2/setup-msys2@v2` step (`msystem: ${{matrix.msys}}`, `install: mingw-w64-${{matrix.msysenv}}-gcc ...`), yet lines 134-135 and 146-147 still set them.

Only the two MinGW/GCC jobs move to windows-2025, while every other Windows job stays on windows-2019, so Windows artefacts in one release are now built on different runner images. Lines 68, 78, 88, 98, 108 and 117 still use `os: windows-2019`; the diff changes only lines 127 and 139 to `windows-2025`. Nothing in the diff explains the split.
